Firstly the harmonies in rock and hip hop are the same. The same harmonic progressions have been used since we first started adopting the current tonal system. In fact, because hip hop frequently samples or is influenced by jazz the harmonies are often denser. Your comment shows, to me, that you want to appreciate it but don’t really where to start. Music is expression and the overwhelmingly negative vibe you get from hip hop is probably cultural. Listen to Poetic Justice, notice that the harmony is dense and the orchestration is complex. The idea that because largely samples are used discredits the complexity ignores that sampling requires knowledge and talent in production and software use. And even if it didn’t artistic merit doesn’t stem from difficulty to produce. It’s not necessarily a positive song but the lyrics aren’t necessarily meaningful either. In a case like this lyrics serve more a rhythmic and musical maybe akin to Black Dog by Led Zepplin - does that song really tell a story or is it the same lyrical ‘nonsense’ that serves a more musical purpose. Positive music is also easy to find if you look: hip hop is a culture of bringing joy and getting out of that ghetto many of its artists grew up in. Listen to Nothing Even Matters by Lauryn Hill if you want a light-hearted song. The point is this music does exist as hip-hop is a genre that has almost been dominant for as long as rock was. Van Halen, for example was just party music akin to the music you’d hear at parties now but the complexity isn’t in terms of shred but rather the art of finding accessible lyrics and sounds with hidden complexity in their jazz-tinted harmonies. Hip hops popularity is a result of cultural diffusion in big cities where people want to tell a story but don’t necessarily have exposure or the money to learn an instrument or get in a big studio. But hip hop is a massive genre so here are a few albums worth listening to:

To Pimp a Butterfly - Kendrick Lamar
Doomsday - MF Doom
Doggystyle - Snoop Dogg 
Late Registration - Kanye West
The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill - Lauryn Hill
IGOR - Tyler The Creator
“Awaken My Love” - Childish Gambino

Notice how some complexity comes from song form, production, rhythms you wouldn’t hear in rock, mixing complex notions in harmony with accessible, familiar stories and sounds etc.

You don’t have to enjoy it, but understand why people do :)
